name: Firecrawl
verdict: No OAuth app exists. Each customer pastes an API key from their Firecrawl dashboard; you store it encrypted and validate it with one test call, or you can call Firecrawl with your own key.
needGuide: No — just collect an API key (API Keys page), or use your own key.

auth.detail: Authorization: Bearer fc-... API key. Basic keyless use exists with per-IP daily caps. The hosted MCP server has three modes: keyless (Search, Scrape, Parse), OAuth sign-in at https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth where the user approves a team, or an API key at https://mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp. No developer-registered OAuth is documented.

approval.gate: None. Firecrawl is a service you call with your own key; a customer-facing connect step is only needed if customers should use their own team. Production needs a paid plan once free credits (1,000) or rate limits are exceeded.

scopes.why: No scopes: a key has the team's full API access.
scopes.summary: No scopes; a key has the team's full API access. MCP OAuth and API key reach the same tools on the team's plan.

cost: Free plan with 1,000 credits; paid tiers Hobby, Standard, Growth, Scale; Enterprise
prerequisites: Account and owner: Any team member with dashboard access creates keys; use a company-owned team. Rate limits are per team and shared across all keys.
Where you register: Create a free account, then open the API Keys page of the dashboard
Cost: Free plan with 1,000 credits; paid tiers Hobby, Standard, Growth, Scale; Enterprise

registerAt.path: Create a free account, then open the API Keys page of the dashboard

steps.do: Create a company Firecrawl account and team
Create an API key on the API Keys page; store it as a server secret
Call /scrape with Authorization: Bearer using the official SDK
If using MCP, point the client at mcp.firecrawl.dev/v2/mcp-oauth and test sign-in and revoke
Upgrade to a plan sized to expected concurrency and add 429 backoff
For customer-owned accounts, add an API key paste field and validate with a cheap call

roles.team: Any team member with dashboard access creates keys; use a company-owned team. Rate limits are per team and shared across all keys.
roles.console: none documented (team roles not covered in the pages read)
roles.customer: For the MCP OAuth path the user signs in to Firecrawl and approves a team; connections can be reviewed and revoked in MCP settings. Otherwise customers paste their own key.

testing: Use the free account or the keyless mode.
Free plan limits: 2 concurrent browsers, 10 scrapes/min, 2 crawls/min; exceeding returns HTTP 429.

blockers.problem: Rate limits are per team and shared across all keys
blockers.fix: New keys do not add capacity.

blockers.problem: Keyless mode is capped per IP per day
blockers.fix: Do not rely on it in production.

blockers.problem: No third-party OAuth app registration documented
blockers.fix: Use pasted keys or the MCP OAuth path.

blockers.problem: Scraped targets can block or have ToS limits

automation.agentCan: Write the SDK calls, 429 handling and the MCP configuration, run test scrapes, and add key validation.
automation.humanMust: Create the account, choose and pay for a plan, and approve MCP OAuth sign-in as a user.

uncertain: Whether Firecrawl will register OAuth apps for third parties, team role details, and numeric keyless limits.
Fetching was cut off before some pages could be checked.
